title: feat(smtp): greylisting with SPF whitelist bypass
description:
## Why

Greylisting is the cheapest effective spam filter: unknown (client_ip, sender, recipient) triplets get a 451 on first contact, forcing legitimate MTAs (which retry) through while most spam bots do not retry. SPF-passing senders are whitelisted immediately — no 451 for Gmail, Fastmail, etc. — so legitimate mail is not delayed.

## Design

### SQLite schema (new migration in stoa-smtp, stored in smtp store pool)

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS greylist (
    client_ip  TEXT    NOT NULL,
    sender     TEXT    NOT NULL,
    recipient  TEXT    NOT NULL,
    first_seen INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime("%s","now")),
    passed     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    last_seen  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime("%s","now")),
    PRIMARY KEY (client_ip, sender, recipient)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_greylist_cleanup ON greylist (last_seen);
```

`passed=1` means the triplet has served its delay and is permanently whitelisted until pruned.

### SPF early evaluation (MAIL FROM time)

Currently SPF runs at DATA time. Move SPF-only evaluation to MAIL FROM:

1. Add `spf_pass: bool` field to `SessionState::Mail` and `SessionState::Rcpt`.
2. At MAIL FROM: call `verify_spf_only(authenticator, client_ip, mail_from, ehlo_domain)` — a thin wrapper around `authenticator.verify_spf(SpfParameters::verify_mail_from(...))`. Store result in state.
3. `verify_spf_only` is async but cheap (one DNS TXT lookup, cached after 41l0/cs5p land). The MAIL FROM response is held until SPF resolves.
4. At DATA: skip the SPF step in `verify_inbound` if SPF was already run; reuse the stored result for DMARC evaluation.

### Greylist check (RCPT TO time)

```
At RCPT TO:
  if spf_pass → write_half.write_all(b"250 OK\r\n") // bypass
  else:
    check_greylist(pool, client_ip, from, to_addr, min_delay_secs)
    → GreylistVerdict::Pass    → 250 OK, mark passed=1 in DB
    → GreylistVerdict::Defer   → 451 4.7.1 Greylisted — try again later\r\n
    → GreylistVerdict::Unknown → INSERT row, return 451
```

`check_greylist` is a single SQL query:
```sql
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO greylist (client_ip, sender, recipient) VALUES (?,?,?);
UPDATE greylist SET last_seen=strftime("%s","now")
  WHERE client_ip=? AND sender=? AND recipient=?;
SELECT passed, first_seen FROM greylist
  WHERE client_ip=? AND sender=? AND recipient=?;
```
If `passed=1` → Pass. If `first_seen < now - min_delay` → update `passed=1`, return Pass. Otherwise → Defer.

### SessionState changes

```rust
enum SessionState {
    // ...
    Mail {
        ehlo_domain: String,
        from: String,
        spf_pass: bool,   // ← new
    },
    Rcpt {
        ehlo_domain: String,
        from: String,
        to: Vec<String>,
        spf_pass: bool,   // ← new; carried forward for DATA reuse
    },
}
```

### Config

```toml
[greylist]
enabled = false          # off by default
min_delay_secs = 300     # 5 minutes
max_age_days = 30        # prune passed entries older than this
```

`enabled = false` default: greylisting is opt-in. When disabled, the RCPT TO handler is unchanged.

### Startup sweep

On server start, before accepting connections:
```sql
DELETE FROM greylist WHERE passed=0 AND last_seen < strftime("%s","now") - 86400;
DELETE FROM greylist WHERE passed=1 AND last_seen < strftime("%s","now") - (max_age_days * 86400);
```
No background task required.

### DATA pipeline integration

`verify_inbound` gains an `Option<SpfOutput>` parameter — if Some (SPF already run at MAIL FROM), it skips the SPF DNS call and feeds the cached result directly into DMARC evaluation. If None (auth disabled or greylist disabled), it runs SPF as before. This avoids a double DNS lookup.

## What stays the same

- Per-connection concurrency unchanged
- DKIM and DMARC still run at DATA time
- Sessions without `auth` configured are unaffected
- SPF-passing senders see zero latency change (no 451, no DB write on the fast path)

## Acceptance criteria

- First contact from unknown triplet → 451
- Retry before min_delay → 451
- Retry after min_delay → 250; row marked passed=1
- Subsequent contacts from same triplet → 250 (no delay)
- SPF-passing sender → 250 immediately, no greylist DB write
- `greylist.enabled = false` → behaviour identical to today
- Startup sweep removes unretried deferred entries older than 24h
- cargo fmt + clippy -D warnings + cargo test --workspace clean
notes: COORDINATION: greylisting bypass depends on connection_whitelisted: bool being passed into run_session. This flag is set true by either stoa-1d9d418c (manual CIDR whitelist) or stoa-da2b926b (DNSWL hit). mgzn must NOT add its own flag — it reads the existing one. Ensure na4h or 1d63 has landed before implementing the bypass path. If neither has landed yet, add the parameter as part of mgzn and leave a TODO comment referencing both epics so they reuse it rather than duplicating.
design: smtp store pool (pool param in run_session) — no new DB file. SPF moved to MAIL FROM time; result carried in SessionState::Mail/Rcpt as spf_pass: bool. verify_inbound gains Option<SpfOutput> to skip double SPF lookup. Startup sweep on server init, no background task.
